title: Deriving the Cofunction Identity cos(x - pi/2) = sin x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the trigonometric addition formulas to derive the identity \cos(x - \pi/2) = \sin x.

steps.title: Rewrite as a Sum and Apply the Cosine Addition Formula
steps.explanation: Expand cos(x + (-pi/2)) using the cosine sum identity cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B with A = x and B = -pi/2.
steps.why: The cosine addition formula holds for all real angles A and B.

steps.title: Evaluate Cosine and Sine at -pi/2
steps.explanation: On the unit circle, the angle -pi/2 points straight down to (0, -1), giving cos(-pi/2) = 0 and sin(-pi/2) = -1.
steps.why: The terminal point of -pi/2 on the unit circle is (0, -1).

steps.title: Substitute and Simplify
steps.explanation: Substitute the numerical values into the expanded expression to obtain sin x.
steps.why: Multiplying by 0 annihilates the first term and subtracting -sin x yields +sin x.
